newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - GM '97 EPS estimates cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - GM '97 EPS estimates cut.

text.p: Furman Selz analyst Maryanne Keller said she cut her 1997 full-year earnings estimate for General Motors Corp to $7.15 a share from $7.80 after the automaker disclosed that strikes will cut second quarter earnings by $490 million, or $0.67 a share. GM earned $6.08 a share in 1996.
-- Keller said she cut her second quarter estimate to $1.95 a share from $2.60. GM earned $2.65 in the 1996 second quarter.

-- Keller said the continuing strike at GM's Pontiac, Mich., full-size-truck plant accounted for more than 60 percent of the 96,000 GM vehicles lost to production due to the strikes. Many of those trucks are high-profit extended-cab versions. The plant normally builds 1,100 full-size trucks a day.
-- If the strike extends into mid-July, Keller said it will have an effect on her third quarter estimate.
